messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#12345 — Escalation policy 'prod-critical' — Trigger: inference-runtime-eastus high 5xx rate

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD12345 created by monitoring@pagerduty (threshold breach). Priority: P1. Service: inference-runtime-eastus.

maria (oncall): ack'd. pulling up metrics now. seeing a spike in 502 and 504 from the inference API. 10% error rate for the last 1m.

alyssa (sre): looking. can you post the runbook link?

maria (oncall): runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/inference/502s (copying snippet)

jordan (eng): thanks. quick check: any recent deploys?

maria (oncall): none in last 30m. autoscaler did a scale-up roughly 3m ago.

mike (eng): logs show repeated LRU eviction warnings and gRPC timeouts to the model backend. past few minutes: latency > 800ms on kv-cache calls.

alyssa (sre): that smells like KV cache saturation. can we toggle cache-ttl and reduce concurrent contexts?

maria (oncall): attempting temporary throttling config: `rlimit.concurrency = 60 -> 40` on inference-router for eastus. patching now.

incident-bot: maria (oncall) updated service config: rlimit.concurrency changed to 40.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation check: primary ack present. No escalation triggered. (timer started)

maria (oncall): small improvement: 502 down from 10% to 6% in 30s. still seeing spikes on long-horizon prompts.

jordan (eng): can we fallback model to smaller variant for public traffic? we have a compatible quantized variant (q3).

mike (eng): we can route new requests to model-v1-q3 but need to avoid disrupting active KV cache. recommend splitting by route: `/api/generate` new routing.

alyssa (sre): agree. implement gradual canary: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback.

maria (oncall): starting canary. adding 10% traffic to model-v1-q3.

incident-bot: PD escalation alarm: primary ack active. secondary timer will fire at +2m if no further updates.

maria (oncall): canary at 10% — 502s down to 4.2% in 45s. good signal.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation policy evaluated: since ack exists, no manager escalation.

kevin (manager): pinging in — saw the PD page. any user impact?

maria (oncall): customers may have experienced intermittent failures for 2-6 minutes depending on locality. error budget hit is small but visible for a few high-volume customers. working mitigation now.

jordan (eng): can we disable continuous batching (it causes long leader waits under saturation) temporarily? it's a toggle at router-level: `batching.enabled = true -> false`

mike (eng): disabling batching will raise CPU but reduce head-of-line blocking. I can flip and monitor.

maria (oncall): doing it now on eastus primary nodes.

incident-bot: maria (oncall) changed batching.enabled -> false on cluster inference-router-eastus.

maria (oncall): immediate drop: 502s -> 1.1% within 20s. latency stable at ~200ms.

kevin (manager): great. what's next for durable fix?

alyssa (sre): follow-ups: 1) investigate KV cache sizing and eviction policy; 2) validate autoscaler thresholds; 3) test continuous batching under load; 4) consider model-variant routing policy to prefer quantized variant during spikes.

jordan (eng): I'll open a ticket with profiling traces and a patch to add graceful ramp for batching.

maria (oncall): are we going to close the PD incident or keep it open for postmortem? customers still saw transient errors but mitigation is successful.

kevin (manager): keep it open until we have RCA and mitigation plan. notify customers in status page.

mike (eng): status page draft: "We experienced intermittent generation errors in eastus for ~6 minutes; mitigation applied (temporary throttling and disabling continuous batching). We're investigating cache eviction root cause and will follow up."

maria (oncall): posting to status now.

incident-bot: Status update posted to status.redwood.ai — Incident PD12345 — message id: st-9876

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: if primary oncall becomes unresponsive, escalation to secondary will occur at +5m. current timers: primary acknowledged 0m ago.

maria (oncall): i'll stay on the thread for 30m for monitoring handoff. if anything flares I'll escalate.

alyssa (sre): thanks. I'm capturing traces and will attach to the PD incident.

jordan (eng): adding temporary model-routing rule to avoid leader KV hotspots — pushing change to canary for validation.

mike (eng): validated change in canary. no negative signal. ready for prod roll.

maria (oncall): rolling routing change to 100% now.

incident-bot: Routing rule rollout started: inference-router-eastus -> model-v1-q3 100% (canary -> prod).

maria (oncall): routing rollout complete; error rate stable at ~0.2% now.

kevin (manager): ok to start incident postmortem. assign to eng-jordan and alyssa.

maria (oncall): assigning. I'll also convert this PD incident to a long-running ticket for RCA.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD12345 status: acknowledged by maria (oncall). current state: monitoring.

maria (oncall): closing Slack thread — will keep PD open until RCA done. Thanks everyone :clap: 

alyssa (sre): good job team. follow-ups: RFC for batching toggles + KV cache sizing — assigning owners in the ticket.

jordan (eng): adding notes to ticket: kernel traces, eviction logs, autoscaler dump.

maria (oncall): last check: 5m steady, ops metrics look green. I'll hand off to next shift at 02:00 UTC.

incident-bot: PD escalation timers reset. Monitoring continues.
